findings.claim: The rear seam at 2:4|2:5 is decided by a tier-3 single-witness petuchah rather than by the tier-1 signal available in the adjacent verse's own bytes.
findings.grounds: boundary_rationale closes the row 'where a petuchah break is recorded (oshb:Isa.2.4, single-witness, tier-3)' and names the mark before the imperative; strongest_rejected_alternative makes the mark the because-clause ('was rejected because a petuchah break is recorded at the close of verse 4'); device_notes then uses it to defeat the row's own disclosed rival — 'the petuchah break at verse 4 is preferred here as the stronger, more local disclosure signal' — over the house-of-Jacob catchword bracketing 2:2-5. The mark itself checks out: the staged parashah inventory records Isa.2.4 as PE (type correct, PE not conflated with SAMEKH, single-witness disclosed), but in the Prophets that layer is tier-3 weak corroboration and never a boundary driver. The tier-1 signal that does stand in bytes at this seam is the verse-initial imperative-vocative of the next verse, “בֵּ֖ית יַעֲקֹ֑ב לְכ֥וּ וְנֵלְכָ֖ה” (oshb:Isa.2.5, tokens 1-4, byte tier), which the neighbour row M8-Isa-010 argues as its own opening and which this row mentions only as an unquoted afterthought.
findings.proposed_change: Re-ground the rear-seam warrant and the rejected_alternative on the verse-initial imperative-vocative at oshb:Isa.2.5 (byte tier), demote the Isa.2.4 petuchah to disclosed tier-3 corroboration, and add oshb:Isa.2.5 to boundary_evidence_refs. No span change.

findings.claim: observed_substrate_signals encodes a tier-3 mark as a boundary signal via the key parashah.pe_boundary.
findings.grounds: The key names the Isa.2.4 PE recorded in the staged parashah inventory, a tier-3 single-witness object. Sibling rows in the same corpus use the corroboration-suffixed form for the identical object class (M8-Isa-017 carries parashah.pe_corroboration and parashah.samekh_corroboration), so two incompatible labellings of one tier-3 layer ship side by side. Recorded for adjudication, not resolved here: the audit brief bars parashah.* keys outright while the shared toolkit's oss field contract lists parashah.*-style keys as sanctioned.
findings.proposed_change: Rename to parashah.pe_corroboration as a dependent field of the driver swap above; route the brief-vs-toolkit conflict on parashah.* to adjudication.

findings.claim: The opening formula is presented as the verse's onset without disclosing that the splice starts at token 2.
findings.grounds: boundary_rationale: 'Opens with the eschatological formula “בְּאַחֲרִ֣ית הַיָּמִ֗ים” (oshb:Isa.2.2, byte tier)'. The splice re-collates at byte tier at that ref, but oshb:Isa.2.2 opens with “וְהָיָ֣ה” (token 1, byte tier); the spliced run stands at tokens 2-3. Sibling rows disclose token positions for exactly this reason (M8-Isa-010 'tokens 2-3'; M8-Isa-021 'token 2').
findings.proposed_change: Either extend the splice to include token 1 or add the token position to the citation.

findings.claim: The shared 2:11|2:12 seam is argued incompatibly by the two rows that own it: the neighbour concedes a live rival against the seam that this row does not concede.
findings.grounds: M8-Isa-011, which owns the same seam as its opening edge, records in device_notes: 'That link leaves a live rival unstated: one sustained pride-and-humbling poem running from 2:9 through 2:17, with the refrain as internal punctuation rather than a row-cutting seam.' This row owns the same seam as its closing edge, presents the identical cross-seam device as neutral texture, and confines its strongest_rejected_alternative to the 2:5-22 whole-complex rival. The device is byte-true and straddles the seam: “וַיִּשְׁפַּל” (oshb:Isa.2.9, token 3, byte tier), “וְשַׁ֖ח” (oshb:Isa.2.11, token 5, byte tier), “וְשָׁפֵֽל” (oshb:Isa.2.12, token 12, byte tier), “וְשַׁח֙” (oshb:Isa.2.17, token 1, byte tier). Cross-seam cohesion law makes a byte-true device straddling a row's own seam an argument for continuity unless the row disposes of it.
findings.proposed_change: Name the 2:9-2:17 sustained-poem rival in this row's own rival disclosure and answer it, or record the closing seam as frontier. No span change proposed.

findings.claim: A single digit is attached to a chain the row itself defines across two different roots, and the digit counts only one of them; the count object is never named.
findings.grounds: device_notes: 'A low/bow root chain also runs through the stanza: “וַיִּשְׁפַּל” (oshb:Isa.2.9), “וְשַׁ֖ח” (oshb:Isa.2.11), “וְשָׁפֵֽל” (oshb:Isa.2.12), and “וְשַׁח֙” (oshb:Isa.2.17), standing at 10 verses book-wide (sweep: 10 verses, skeleton).' Re-swept: the 10 is the skeleton substring of the LOW root alone, at exactly 10 verses (Isa.2.9, 2.11, 2.12, 2.17, 5.15, 10.33, 29.4, 32.19, 40.4, 57.15). The BOW member “וְשַׁ֖ח” (spliced from oshb:Isa.2.11 token 5) is a different object entirely — 1 verse at byte, 2 at accent_stripped, 2 at token-exact skeleton, 4 as a skeleton substring — and its bare two-letter skeleton stands at 40 verses, the short-token trap the campaign hazard catalog names. No digit is offered for it. Semantic-class count discipline requires the swept object be named first; blended sweeps are barred.
findings.proposed_change: Split the claim: give the low-root skeleton object its 10 with the object named, and give the bow-root member its own token-exact digit; or restrict the chain to one root.

findings.claim: The exclusivity claim about what is byte-identical between the two refrain sites is byte-false: the byte-identical run is seven tokens, not the five-token clause named.
findings.grounds: device_notes: 'only the closing ‘Yahweh alone… in that day’ clause is byte-identical at both sites.' Re-collated: the maximal byte-identical tail shared by oshb:Isa.2.11 and oshb:Isa.2.17 is the seven-token run “ר֣וּם אֲנָשִׁ֑ים וְנִשְׂגַּ֧ב יְהוָ֛ה לְבַדּ֖וֹ בַּיּ֥וֹם הַהֽוּא” (byte tier; sweep: 2 verses, byte), not the five-token clause “וְנִשְׂגַּ֧ב יְהוָ֛ה לְבַדּ֖וֹ בַּיּ֥וֹם הַהֽוּא”. The two extra byte-identical tokens belong to the very loftiness-of-man material the same sentence says 'varies in word order'. The staged universals checker flags this same sentence (claims 'only' and 'identical').
findings.proposed_change: Restate the byte-identical extent as the seven-token run, and narrow the word-order variation claim to the head of the loftiness clause.

findings.claim: A verbatim WEB English rendering is cited under an MT witness prefix.
findings.grounds: boundary_rationale: “Yahweh alone will be exalted in that day.” (oshb:Isa.2.11). That string is verbatim WEB Isa 2:11; the bytes at oshb:Isa.2.11 are Hebrew (the row's own splice from that ref is “וְנִשְׂגַּ֧ב יְהוָ֛ה לְבַדּ֖וֹ בַּיּ֥וֹם הַהֽוּא”, byte tier). findings.proposed_change: Re-prefix the gloss to web:Isa.2.11.

findings.claim: The row's opening seam at 2:17|2:18 rests on no ruled tier-1 signal in its own cited verse's bytes, and no tier-3 mark stands there either; the warrant is topical shift alone.
findings.grounds: boundary_rationale grounds the open on 'a fresh topical turn after the stanza-closing refrain of verse 17'; strongest_rejected_alternative confirms it: 'the unit is bounded instead by topical shift (from proud objects to idols and human flight) and the petuchah break closing the chapter.' The cited verse is three tokens in full — “וְהָאֱלִילִ֖ים כָּלִ֥יל יַחֲלֹֽף” (oshb:Isa.2.18, byte tier) — a waw-conjunctive definite noun carrying no frame onset of any ruled class (no hoy, hinneh, koh-amar, neum, massa header, imperative, vocative or temporal formula), and the waw binds it to what precedes. The staged parashah inventory records NO mark at Isa.2.17 or Isa.2.18, so no tier-3 corroboration stands at this seam (absence is not counterevidence, but it leaves the seam unsupported). The row's own observed_substrate_signals — oracle_frame.concluding_summary and parashah.pe_boundary — both attach to the row's CLOSE at 2:22; the row records no opening-seam signal at all. Three further byte facts argue continuity across this seam: the verse-initial temporal formula “בַּיּ֤וֹם הַהוּא֙” stands at oshb:Isa.2.20 (tokens 1-2, byte tier) INSIDE the span, so the only verse-initial temporal-formula onset in the neighbourhood is two verses past the chosen seam and the row mentions it merely as a recurring 'tag'; the flight-from-terror device the row itself discloses runs from oshb:Isa.2.10 (outside, in the 2:5-11 stanza) into oshb:Isa.2.19 and oshb:Isa.2.21 (inside), its four-token core “מִפְּנֵי֙ פַּ֣חַד יְהוָ֔ה וּמֵהֲדַ֖ר” collating byte at oshb:Isa.2.10 and accent_stripped at the two later sites (sweep: 3 verses, accent_stripped); and frontier_flag_considered is false on the weakest-warranted row in this batch.
findings.proposed_change: PROPOSAL ONLY — route the 2:17|2:18 seam to adjudication with three options recorded: (a) respan to fold this material into the preceding refrain-closed stanza, M8-Isa-011 Isa.2.12-Isa.2.17 becoming Isa.2.12-Isa.2.22 as a one-edit seam-pair cure; (b) re-cut this row to Isa.2.20-Isa.2.22 on the verse-initial temporal formula at oshb:Isa.2.20 (byte tier), leaving 2:18-19 with the preceding stanza; (c) retain Isa.2.18-Isa.2.22 but set frontier_flag_considered true, lower confidence, and disclose the tier-1 shortfall at the opening seam. Any replacement warrant must pass the test that killed the original.

The mark checks out — the staged parashah inventory records Isa.2.22 as PE, and boundary_rationale discloses it correctly as single-witness, tier-3 — but in the Prophets the layer never bounds a unit. The tier-1 signal at this rear seam stands in the next verse's bytes, “כִּי֩ הִנֵּ֨ה הָאָד֜וֹן יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֗וֹת” (oshb:Isa.3.1, tokens 1-5, byte tier), which the neighbour row M8-Isa-013 argues as its hinneh-announcement onset and which this row neither quotes nor lists in boundary_evidence_refs.
findings.proposed_change: Re-ground the rear warrant on the hinneh-announcement onset at oshb:Isa.3.1, add that ref to boundary_evidence_refs, demote the Isa.2.22 petuchah to disclosed corroboration, and rename the oss key to parashah.pe_corroboration.

findings.claim: The 22-verse hoy digit is labelled as the onset object, but it is the token-verse object and it includes a verse whose token is a different lexeme.
findings.grounds: device_notes: '(the hoy-onset lexeme stands at 22 verses book-wide, sweep: 22 verses, skeleton)'. Re-swept from the pointed form spliced at oshb:Isa.5.20 token 1, “ה֣וֹי”: skeleton 22 verses / accent_stripped 21 / byte 5. The staged device inventory carries the same split — 22 token-verses against 20 verse-initial — under an explicit role-split-before-counting note separating woe-oracle onsets from the 1:4 indictment, the 1:24 self-exclamation and the 55:1 invitation; by that role split the woe-oracle onset subclass is 18, not 22. The skeleton 22 also carries Isa.16.4, whose token is “מוֹאָ֛ב הֱוִי סֵ֥תֶר” (oshb:Isa.16.4, tokens 4-6, byte tier) — an imperative of the be-verb, not the hoy lexeme. So the named object matches neither the counted object nor the onset subclass. The same sentence's oy work is by contrast exact and is confirmed on re-sweep: token-exact skeleton 4 verses (Isa.3.9, 3.11, 6.5, 24.16) against a bare three-letter substring 8 verses, the extra 4 being Isa.1.24, 26.9, 35.8 and 63.10.
findings.proposed_change: Restate as the token object with its scope and role given — e.g. 22 token-verses book-wide of which 20 are verse-initial — applying to hoy the same object discipline this sentence already applies to oy.

findings.claim: The English introduced as the rendering of the spliced sound-play covers the whole verse, roughly twice the extent of the splice.
findings.grounds: boundary_rationale: 'sealed by the sound-play “וַיְקַ֤ו לְמִשְׁפָּט֙ וְהִנֵּ֣ה מִשְׂפָּ֔ח לִצְדָקָ֖ה וְהִנֵּ֥ה צְעָקָֽה” (oshb:Isa.5.7, byte tier), rendered “For the vineyard of Yahweh of Armies is the house of Israel, and the men of Judah his pleasant plant. He looked for justice, but behold, oppression, for righteousness, but behold, a cry of distress.” (web:Isa.5.7)'. oshb:Isa.5.7 runs 17 tokens; the splice is tokens 11-17 and re-collates at byte tier, while the English is the whole of WEB Isa 5:7 and its first sentence answers tokens 1-10, “כִּ֣י כֶ֜רֶם יְהוָ֤ה צְבָאוֹת֙ בֵּ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וְאִ֣ישׁ יְהוּדָ֔ה נְטַ֖ע שַׁעֲשׁוּעָ֑יו” (byte tier), which is not in the splice. Both texts are verbatim at their own refs; the defect is extent parity.
findings.proposed_change: Cut the gloss to the sound-play clause only, or extend the splice to the full verse; a quote/gloss parity repair re-cuts the gloss.

The claim is substantively supportable — the cohortative spliced at oshb:Isa.5.1 tokens 1-2, “אָשִׁ֤ירָה נָּא֙” (byte tier), has a skeleton standing at exactly 1 verse book-wide — but the object must be named first here, because a bare sing-root skeleton sweep returns 9 verses and blends the ornament homograph “וְהַשֵּׁיר֖וֹת” (oshb:Isa.3.19, token 2, byte tier), which is the earlier hit an unnamed sweep would surface against this very claim.
findings.proposed_change: Add the digit with its count object named, e.g. the cohortative form at 1 verse book-wide (sweep: 1 verse, skeleton), and state the homograph exclusion.

findings.claim: A 497-character device_notes block ships byte-identical on the two rows that face each other across this seam, against the variation order for mandated recurring sentences.
